verdict.rationale: GitHub documents a broad first-party programmatic surface: a REST API for integrations and automation, a GraphQL API with a published schema reference, a stable OpenAPI description of the REST API, versioning with advance notice of breaking changes, and fine-grained token permissions per endpoint. The GitHub CLI also brings pull requests, issues, Actions and other features to the terminal. However, no evidence explicitly claims or demonstrates that every UI capability is available via the API, so parity is implied rather than proven. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, coverage evidence for UI-only areas (e.g. settings, Copilot agent features), and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Create integrations, retrieve data, and automate your workflows with the GitHub REST API.
The GitHub GraphQL API offers more precise and flexible queries than the GitHub REST API.
This repository contains OpenAPI descriptions for GitHub's REST API.
As of the 1.1.4 release, this description is considered stable and generally available.
GitHub CLI is a command-line tool that brings pull requests, issues, GitHub Actions, and other GitHub features to your terminal, so you can do all your work in one place.
